TLDR for you

(Save for later)


Step 1: Start with the problem

Frame the human problem your product solves without brand names.

Examples: "My baby won't eat solid foods"



Step 2: Pull real convos in Reddit Answers

Example prompt: "Show me what people on Reddit are saying about staying hydrated. Are there recurring words, frustrations, or emotional tones when people discuss electrolyte powders?"



Step 3: Extract quotes

Tag emotional lines with hooks in a spreadsheet.

Quote: "I always end up dehydrated on flights no matter how much water I drink"
Emotion: Frustration
Creative Hook: Hydration that lasts

Quote: "Most electrolyte powders taste like medicine"
Emotion: Annoyance
Creative Hook: Electrolytes that don't taste like regret



Step 4: Cluster into angles

Group quotes into patterns like this

Common clusters:
Pain first
Before/After
Tried Everything
Social Proof
Identity/Community
Transformation

Ex: "Most powders taste fake" becomes Pain first. "Finally found one that tastes good" becomes Transformation.



Step 5: Turn quotes into hooks

Feed clusters into ChatGPT with this prompt:

If you want to know why Meta ads die after 3 days, the answer is almost always delivery, not creative fatigue.

A 72-hour collapse isn't a creative problem. It's a delivery signature.

Genuine fatigue shows up after 5 to 14 days, per Search Engine Land. An ad that was healthy on Monday and dead on Thursday hasn't been seen enough times to wear anyone out.

What changes on day three is the algorithm. The first 48 to 72 hours are Meta's exploration window, and when it closes, delivery narrows to whatever the system learned.

Before you diagnose, rule out noise. HyperFX puts roughly 20% of "my ROAS dropped" reports down to mismatched windows or attribution settings.

Then check, in this order:

1. Learning collapse. Under about 50 optimization events in 7 days, the ad set sits in Learning Limited and typically loses 15 to 30%, per HyperFX.
2. A reset you caused. Under Andromeda, a 5 to 10% budget change on day two can restart Learning.
3. Audience exhaustion. CPM up more than 25% in 72 hours with frequency climbing means the audience pocket ran dry. Keep the creative and broaden the audience.

Sometimes it really is the creative. A tight retargeting pool on a big budget can push frequency past 3 in two days, and then CTR falls 20 to 30% from its own baseline.

Segwise's fatigue tracking flags sustained declines against thresholds you set, like a 20% ROAS drop over 7 days, so you can tell a slow creative decline apart from a day-three delivery drop.

If you want to know which creative analytics tool an agency should pick in 2026, the answer is the one that fits your client mix, not the longest feature list.

You're not short on tools. You're short on knowing why Ad A beat Ad B.

Most agencies still report at the ad level. Across hundreds of ads and a dozen client accounts, "which ad won" stops helping by the second client review.

What to match on:

1. Ad networks. Most tools in this category are still Meta-first, so if a client runs on AppLovin, Unity or Mintegral, check the integration list before anything else.
2. Analysis depth. Ad-level reporting tells you what happened. Element-level tagging of the hook, the CTA placement and the visual style tells you why.
3. Client separation. Each client's data needs its own workspace, never blended into one account.
4. Creative volume. The gap between the brief and the finished asset is where agency hours go.

One honest caveat: a deep platform can be more than you need if you run one or two small accounts.

If you want to know whether AI creative can cut your CPI by 70%, the answer is rarely, and almost never from the AI alone.

The 70% you keep seeing is production cost. CPI is a different number.

AI cuts what you spend making variants by 70 to 90%. Genra's 2026 breakdown puts AI video at $0.50 to $30 per minute, against $1,000 to $50,000 for traditional production.

The auction prices the install, not your production bill.

Look at where the big wins actually came from:

- PURE App, -74% CPI: credited mainly to a Moloco DSP partnership
- FET, -66% CPA: AI production plus testing built for subscription conversion
- Star Chef 2, -18% CAC: a testing surface big enough to surface winners

70% isn't fake. PURE App hit it. It just isn't representative.

The number that holds up is smaller. AppsFlyer looked at 1.1 million video creatives and found campaigns running 20+ variants cut CPA by up to 29%, with mixed formats adding another 5%.

Cheap volume has a cost too. Every competitor can now ship 50 to 100 ads a month, and Meta's Andromeda update limits near-duplicates, so fatigue arrives faster.

Your advantage isn't how fast you generate. It's how fast performance data reaches the next round.

That means tagging the hook, CTA, character and voiceover on every ad, mapping each to performance, and catching fatigue before it shows up in CPI. Segwise is built to help with that loop.

If you want to know what sets the best AI creative brief generators apart in 2026, they write the brief from your ad data, not a blank doc.

A creative brief isn't a writing task anymore. It's a data task.

Platform targeting is now mostly automated, so the creative is the main lever you still control. A brief filled in from memory spends that lever on a guess.

"Creative brief generator" actually covers two different jobs:

- A data-backed tool connects to your ad accounts, tags what's inside each creative, and names the hook, angle, format and CTA your own numbers point to.
- A general-purpose writer like ChatGPT or Claude turns a prompt into a clean brief, but it knows nothing about your performance unless you paste it in.
- Most data-backed tools stop at the brief. Only one in our comparison also makes the ad.

The honest part: you may not need a dedicated tool at all. Below roughly $10k a month in spend, a template plus your dashboards is usually enough.

Above that, you're testing dozens of creatives a month across more than one network, and "what should we make next" turns into a weekly question.

That's where Segwise fits. It tags every creative element across 15+ ad networks and MMPs and maps each tag to ROAS and CPI. Its Creative Strategy Agent writes the brief from what's winning, and the Creative Generation Agent helps your team turn that brief into statics, video and playables.

working: Tactical, step-by-step swipe files and workflows generate outsized engagement, seen in Motion's Reddit research workflow post netting 317 likes, 15 comments, and 7 shares.

Specific breakdown teardowns comparing ad angles and delivery mechanics generate consistent engagement, as shown in Atria's UK turmeric teardown earning 3 likes and 3 shares off a small profile baseline.
Speaker roundups featuring known practitioner names capture moderate traction, such as Motion's Chief Marketer SF recap yielding 32 likes.
Podcast and interview cutdowns addressing strategic agency tensions drive modest engagement, exemplified by Hawky's interview on why volume is not creative strategy getting 11 likes.
not_working: Vague product feature laundry lists and generic event booth photo recaps fall flat, seen across Triple Whale's updates getting 11 to 23 likes and almost zero conversation.
Pure feature release announcements and hollow AI buzzwords fail to spark discussion, illustrated by Motion's MCP post getting 14 likes and 0 comments, and Foreplay's MCP launch earning 12 likes.
Unattributed generic claims like 5-in-1 subscriptions or AI avatar checklists struggle for reach, shown by AdGraam's posts getting between 2 and 8 likes with zero comments.
Empty teaser lines without meat or context collapse, such as GoMarble posting empty or near-empty posts with 2 to 3 likes.
moves: Motion is pushing practitioner community events and launching agent tool integrations via MCP under its Runneth branding.
Triple Whale is expanding Moby beyond attribution into end-to-end autonomous task execution across store ops and creative drafting.
Hawky is positioning itself as an agentic media buyer and creative strategist through podcast content attacking brute-force volume.
Foreplay is turning its ad library into an MCP-accessible intelligence layer for LLMs while driving team expansion.
AdGraam is targeting the Indian D2C ecosystem with fast-turnaround AI UGC avatars and multi-tool consolidation.
Atria is pushing autonomous ad generation and creative intelligence through its Slack agent Raya.
Segwise is anchoring its messaging on deep element-level attribution to diagnose early ad fatigue against platform delivery anomalies.
GoMarble is pushing conversational ad analysis and Perplexity-style creative research assistants.
